---
title: "Step 0 — Setup new project"
---

Stand up a new PTI project on disk: install the package, scaffold the project folder, and understand the layout you'll be filling in over Steps 1–6.

This step uses Rwanda as the worked example country. The scaffolded project is a complete, working Rwanda PTI app — render the pipeline as-is to see it work end-to-end, then replace the Rwanda inputs with your own country.

## Install devPTIpack

`devPTIpack` is a GitHub-hosted R package. Install it with `pak`:

```r
#| eval: false
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("worldbank/devPTIpack")
library(devPTIpack)
```

The pipeline renders a data-quality report in Step 5. The HTML version always renders; the companion PDF needs a LaTeX engine. To enable the PDF on a fresh R install:

```r
#| eval: false
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

LaTeX is optional — the pipeline skips the PDF with a warning when no LaTeX engine is on `PATH`, and the HTML report is produced either way.

## Scaffold the project folder — `create_new_pti()`

[`create_new_pti(path)`](../reference/create_new_pti.html) copies the bundled
`template_pti` skeleton to `path`, creating that directory if it does not exist
and prompting before overwriting if it does. It then:

- replaces the `{{APP_NAME}}` placeholder throughout the scaffold with the project folder name, and
- prints a numbered next-steps banner so you know exactly what to do next.

Inside RStudio or Positron it also offers to open the new folder as a project.

```r
#| eval: false
create_new_pti("~/projects/my_pti")
```

What lands on disk:

- The numbered pipeline files (`00-master.R` through `06-deploy.R`) wired to render Rwanda end-to-end.
- The Quarto website scaffold (`_quarto.yml`, `app-page.qmd`) and the data-quality report (`05-compile-report.qmd`).
- A working `app.R` that loads from `app-data/` paths, and a `landing-page.md` you edit before deploying.
- A `sample-data/` folder with the raw Rwanda inputs the pipeline ingests.
- A `CHECKLIST.md` — a two-phase checklist (before first run / before deployment).
- An empty `app-data/` folder that the pipeline fills as you render Steps 1–5.

## Annotated folder structure

```
my_pti/
│
├── README.md                       # File order + tutorial links
├── CHECKLIST.md                    # Before-first-run / before-deploy checklist
├── 00-master.R                     # Pipeline orchestrator (Steps 1, 3, 4, 5 + report + website)
│
├── 01-shapes.qmd                   # Step 1 — load + validate boundaries, build hex grid
├── 02a-user-zonal-stats.qmd        # Step 2 — OPTIONAL stub; user-driven raster extracts
├── 03-user-data.qmd                # Step 3 — merge indicator data into the metadata workbook
├── 04-hex-data.qmd                 # Step 4 — pull H3 hex indicators from Space2Stats
├── 05-compile.qmd                  # Step 5 — compile_pti_data() merges + validates
├── 05-compile-report.qmd           # Step 5 — data-quality report (HTML + PDF)
├── 06-deploy.R                     # Step 6 — manual deployment script
│
├── _quarto.yml                     # Quarto website config (renders docs/)
├── app-page.qmd                    # "Live app" page of the docs/ website
├── app.R                           # Shiny entry point — DEPLOYED
├── landing-page.md                 # App About-tab content — DEPLOYED
│
├── sample-data/                    # Rwanda raw inputs (replace with your own)
│   ├── rwa_adm0.geojson            # country boundary
│   ├── rwa_adm1.geojson            # 5 provinces
│   ├── rwa_adm2.geojson            # 30 districts
│   ├── sample-metadata-adm1.xlsx   # synthetic Adm1-only indicators (simple)
│   └── sample-metadata-adm1-adm2.xlsx  # synthetic Adm1+Adm2 (multi-level)
│
├── app-data/                       # Pipeline outputs — DEPLOYED
│   ├── shapes.rds                  # output of Step 1
│   ├── metadata-user.xlsx          # output of Step 3 (intermediate)
│   ├── metadata-hex.xlsx           # output of Step 4 (intermediate)
│   ├── metadata.xlsx               # output of Step 5 (canonical)
│   ├── pti-metadata.html           # output of Step 5 (data-quality report)
│   ├── pti-metadata.pdf            # output of Step 5 (when LaTeX is available)
│   └── shapefiles.zip              # output of Step 5
│
├── docs/                           # Data-quality website — built by Step 5
├── data-raw/                       # Re-runnable scripts that produced sample-data/
└── R/                              # golem boilerplate
```

The deployment bundle is **`app.R` + `landing-page.md` + `app-data/` only** — everything else is build-time scaffolding. The `docs/` website deploys separately (see [Step 6](build-pti-6-deploy.html)).

## How `00-master.R` fits in

`00-master.R` is the pipeline orchestrator. It renders the step `.qmd` files top-to-bottom via `quarto::quarto_render()`; each step writes into `app-data/`, and downstream steps read from there. It finishes by rendering the data-quality report and the `docs/` website.

```r
#| eval: false
source("00-master.R")
```

By default it runs Steps 1, 3, 4, and 5, plus the report and website. Step 2 (optional zonal stats) ships commented out; Step 6 (deploy) is always manual. The top of the script also holds two switches — `HEX_RESOLUTION` and `INCLUDE_HEX_IN_APP` — and the `APP_URL` you fill in once the app is deployed. Comment or uncomment lines to skip optional steps, or to drop in your own additions (e.g. an `02b-` zonal-stats extract). Treat `00-master.R` as a recipe you edit, not a black box.

## ⚠ `app-data/` and git — decide consciously

`app-data/` holds the deployment-ready compiled artefacts. Whether you check it into git is a deliberate decision:

- **Track it** if your data is non-sensitive and small enough to live in a repo. Useful for reviewer reproducibility.
- **Ignore it** (`echo "app-data/" >> .gitignore`) if the data is sensitive, large, or both. This is the conservative default for World Bank deployments.

Don't let it slip through unreviewed. `app-data/` is what you deploy — if it's in git, your repository is publishing the same files Posit Connect serves. The same caution applies to `docs/`, which contains rendered HTML built from your data.

## Sample data — run as-is first

Before swapping in your own country, render the template against the bundled Rwanda data:

```r
#| eval: false
source("00-master.R")
shiny::runApp("app.R")
```

You should see a working PTI dashboard with 5 Rwandan provinces, 30 districts, and 3 synthetic indicators across two pillars, plus a `docs/` data-quality website. This sanity-checks your install — every dependency, every binding, every read/write path — before you change anything. (Step 4 fetches data from World Bank Space2Stats, so the first run needs internet access; comment out the Step 4 line in `00-master.R` to run fully offline.)

Once that works, replace `sample-data/rwa_*.geojson` with your country's boundaries (Step 1) and `sample-data/sample-metadata-*.xlsx` with your indicator workbook (Step 3).
